pr_body:
In TileData, this PR renames `texture_offset` to `texture_origin` as it is a bit better name and avoids confusion.

Also, it unclamps it. It was previously forbidding values that would put the base tile (like, the tile on the grid) outside of the drawn region. It is now possible to use any kind of value, but that meant I had to modify the tile atlas view to avoid a mess.
Now, positions in the tile atlas editor get displayed only if they fit the texture region. Otherwise, the value is displayed as text:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6093119/214912027-dcf4ddc3-5964-4160-a41c-654e58f1d344.mp4


Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/68277.


It's not super urgent for 4.0, but since it renames something, and cleans up things a bit, I think it might be worth merging.
pr_comments: The classref needs to be synced too.

I think it's worth breaking compat now to clarify, but for the sake of existing users, you should likely add some compatibility code in TileSet by overriding `_set` and `_get` to handle existing serialized values for `texture_offset`.

issue_context.title: TileMap: Updating texture_offset in _tile_data_runtime_update() has no effect
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

v4.0.beta3.official [01ae26d31]

### System information

Windows 10

### Issue description

Changing the texture offset in the runtime TileData in _tile_data_runtime_update() does nothing, since in draw_tile() the texture_offset from the runtime TileData is ignored:

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/ec521a405a89a1b80a9989c09dcc2f2e7763ddcf/scene/2d/tile_map.cpp#L1369-L1375


### Steps to reproduce

Create a TileMap
Update a cell's TileData texture_offset in _tile_data_runtime_update(). The tile's position will not change.

### Minimal reproduction project

[RuntimeTileData.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/9942845/RuntimeTileData.zip)
comments:
You example project clearly shows a mistake, assuming that `_tile_data_runtime_update` is ran every frame. 
This method is in fact only called when you set/update a tile, otherwise it would cause huge performance issues.

This method can be useful, but it should definitely be not used to animate tiles in a complex way (like, more complex than what the built-in tileset animation system provides). Instead, you should use a TileSetSceneCollectionSource, and paint scenes on your tilemap.

The example project calls force_update() in _process(), you can add a line to change the modulate and you can see it will change while the offset does not.
I agree TileSetSceneCollectionSource is probably a better solution for animating tile movement, but I still think it should be possible to alter offsets per tile, one example (non animation related) use case being to slightly offset tiles for visual effect:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10264470/200434071-ff121090-3a3e-496a-ac96-f7d0962ae016.png)

I guess know what is wrong. You assume that texture_offset will move the texture in the TileMap rendering, while it is not really how it works.

The texture_offset property is used to set the origin when tiles are wider than a single cell, which is possible only by defining what I call "big tiles" in an atlas. Typically, when you have a tree taking several cell, you want the base of the tree being the origin.
In your example project, you are not using a big tile, so the texture_offset gets clamped to (0, 0), since there's is not really an origin to set.

Here I modified your example project with a base grid of 64x64 instead, and created a "big tile" instead:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6093119/200514393-1f615df0-0d1d-4683-bf9e-7ff7f1d36892.mp4

In the end I think that maybe the restriction could be lifted, at the price of maybe a confusing UI when you have weird origins sets (the origins might overlap in the property painting panel. But I guess we could find a workaround.

I used "tile_tex_offset" in godot v3.5 to create a tile bouncing effect when the player hits it from below like in a Mario game. But I ran into this issue when migrating my project to v4. I believe that this restriction should be lifted.

AFAIK this is the only mechanism we have (barring TileSetScenesCollectionSource) to dynamically position a tile separately from the collision shapes defined in its physics layers. Please correct me if I'm wrong (I'd really like to do this another way for my use case).

I'm making a top-down 2D game with a pseudo height dimension. "Height" is implemented as rendering the sprite at a Y offset. I want to implement physics so all collision shapes are placed at "sea level", but the corresponding sprites can be rendered at any "height". This simplifies collision logic between objects at different heights, e.g. when stairs are involved. But I also want to use tilemaps at different heights. For this to work I need some way to e.g. render a tilemap at a certain height but send the collision shapes to "sea level". In Godot 3 I used `TileSet.tile_set_texture_offset(...)` to achieve this, and that's the maximum amount of hacking around I'm willing to do. If there really is no other way in Godot 4, I'd like this restriction lifted.

EDIT: alternatively bring back `tile_set_shape_offset` from Godot 3 :)

> @groud BTW I think the name of the property and the behavior are reversed. For positive texture_offset I'd expect the tile to be visually shifted right/down (also that's how it works in 3.x). Currently it would be shifted left/up instead because as mentioned it's the offset of the texture origin, hence the visible texture offset is the opposite. So I suggest either renaming this property or reversing its behavior.

Yeah, I guess it could be renamed "texture_origin" I guess. But I feel it's a bit late now.

> Even without a workaround I'd say a confusing UI is better than lack of the feature many users require / rely on. UI can always be improved later (e.g. based on the feedback of some angry users smile).

Users should not rely on that though. Animating such a value is super inefficient and should be done with a scene instead. I am not strictly against it but it is not of very high priority TBH.

review_comments: Usually we also handle `_get`. Not sure if it's strictly needed but that's what we normally do :P

Hmm, that was not done for TileSet before (like, even in 3.x code). So I assumed it was only done in getters everywhere.

But well, I added it anyway.
`_get` is only needed for script compatibility. If you handle only `_set`, at least your scene/resource will load without losing data (like in #71347).

> `_get` is only needed for script compatibility. If you handle only `_set`, at least your scene/resource will load without losing data (like in #71347).

Yeah that's what I was thinking too. I am not sure a lot of people would set `texture_offset` without using the property (thus using `set(...)`)but I guess that's fine anyway.
